analysis_notes.provenance: Repost of a Chinese 2D stick-figure horror animation series (village / 'Tulou' goat-monster arc) with English TTS dub and burned-in English captions; this clip is a mid-series part that starts and ends mid-scene. Study structure only, never the story (BRIEF rule 5).

title_pattern.notes: Zero-information title. Discovery is 100% For You feed; the hashtags borrow the huge anime/edit audience even though the content is a Chinese stick-figure horror cartoon. The first spoken line does all the title's work. For our channel: on TikTok/Shorts the caption can be hashtags; on YouTube we still need a real title.
title_pattern.copyable: Tag into an adjacent big-audience category (#anime #animation #horrorstory #storytime) and let the hook carry; a series label like 'Part 7' is absent here, which hides that it's mid-series and lowers drop-off from 'I missed part 1'.

thumbnail.why_it_works: On TikTok the cover barely matters (autoplay). What it does convey: an urgent action mid-sentence (open loop in the caption), visible fear on a simple readable face, and a moody horror palette. In a profile grid the caption-in-black-bar look signals 'narrated story series'.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: All scrambled onto the roof, and mom hurried up the ladder right behind us. That's when grandma rolled out in her wheelchair, screaming in terror. Huzzy! Huzzy!
hook.device: In-medias-res cold open: no context, characters already fleeing an unseen threat; a helpless victim (grandma in wheelchair) screaming a name; immediate moral dilemma (who goes back for her?). Narration at ~350 wpm fills every frame. Within 15 s a family-betrayal conflict (husband + mistress vs wife) is layered on top of the monster threat.
hook.time_to_first_threat_visual: 32 s (monsters); before that the hook is purely human conflict + implied threat
hook.notes: Works because the outrage/drama hook (cheating dad abandons wife and mother) is legible without context, so mid-series viewers don't bounce.

beats.summary: Family is already fleeing onto the roof; grandma left behind screams from her wheelchair. No setup: viewer is dropped into a crisis from a serialized story (this is a mid-series part).
Dad, who is with his mistress, orders Mom back down to care for his mother and threatens divorce; Mom refuses and keeps climbing. Villain-parent setup.
Dad shoves the ladder away; Mom falls flat on her back. Moral outrage spike.
Iron gate smashed; three four-horned goat monsters burst in. Dad and mistress flee across roofs into fog, abandoning kids.
Injured Mom tells the kids to escape via Grandma Li's ladder; monsters circle and make the final attack on Mom and grandma (off-screen kill).
Kids run across rooftops in fog to Grandma Li's house (only unlocked route), climb down.
Grandma Li heard the commotion; kids report the monsters ('look like goats, four horns'); plan to reach village chief's shotgun and phone.
Courtyard gate is ajar in thick fog - 'unknown dread'. Grandma Li silences the kids, creeps over and bolts the gate.
Inside, she reveals a hidden hollow under an 80 cm concrete slab beneath the bed; lore: the creatures (Tulou) are strong, fast and track prey by scent.
Narrator realises Grandma Li knows too much; ties to a 'black bear tragedy 60 years ago' that was really the monsters.
Grandma Li hands over a book of ancient records on the creatures, explains her parents were killed by them, says there's no room for three and someone must lure them away; emotional farewell.
Slab slides shut, darkness, a sliver of light through a crack; boy watches her dump chili and garlic to mask their scent. Cuts off mid-scene: 'Stay inside and don't make a sound.'

pacing.wpm_note: Extremely fast: TTS narration (likely sped-up ~1.4-1.5x) with no pauses; caption chunks change every ~1.2 s (121 cues / 153 s)
pacing.visual_change_rate: new framing roughly every 4 s; within shots there are constant small changes (expression swaps, push-ins, fog drift), so something moves every ~1-2 s
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~10-15 s: ladder shove 25 s, monsters 32 s, Mom's death 49 s, gate ajar 82 s, slab/hiding 100 s, lore reveal 112 s, sacrifice 124 s, cliffhanger 150 s
pacing.structure_ratio: 0-25% betrayal+monster attack, 25-55% escape+refuge, 55-90% lore+mentor sacrifice, final 7% cliffhanger

techniques_worth_copying: Cold open mid-crisis with a human-conflict hook (betrayal, abandonment) before the monster appears - drama is legible with zero context
Layer a domestic villain (cheating, cowardly father) on top of the supernatural threat: viewers rage-watch and comment
First-person child narrator ('my sister and I') - instant vulnerability and sympathy
Monster drawn in a different, more detailed/realistic painted style than the simple round-head cast - the style break itself is scary
Off-screen deaths: show the circling and the lunge, cut to the survivor's face; sound/caption carries the horror

Folk-horror lore drip: named creature (Tulou), rules (fast, strong, tracks by scent; chili and garlic mask scent), a cover-up ('it wasn't a bear 60 years ago'), an old book of ancient records - sets up a series
Mentor sacrifice + entrusted macguffin ('tell the world the truth') to deliver an emotional peak late in the clip
Hiding-place claustrophobia: slab closes, screen goes black, single sliver of light through a crack - POV darkness is cheap and effective
End abruptly mid-scene on an imperative line ('Stay inside and don't make a sound') to drive the next-part follow
Very fast narration (~350 wpm) with 1-line captions that change every ~1.2 s - the eye never rests
Letterboxed 16:9 picture in a 9:16 frame with captions in the top black bar: captions never cover the art, and it reads as 'story series' format
Fog as a constant layer: hides background detail, gives cheap parallax, and is the transition device (fog wipes/dissolves)

code_only_remake_requirements.frame_layout: 1080x1920 black canvas; 16:9 art band (1080x608) centred around y~45%; caption area in black above band (white italic sans ~44px, max 2 lines, centred)
code_only_remake_requirements.characters: SVG paper-doll rig in the round-head stick-figure style: circular white head, hair shape (bob, curly white, messy black), pill-shaped coloured torso, stick limbs; swappable expression sets (fear, anger, sneer, crying with tear streaks, screaming), anime anger-vein and sweat-drop overlays, simple arm poses (point, shove, pat heads). Rig must support profile + 3/4 front views.
code_only_remake_requirements.creature: One detailed SVG/canvas-painted creature (four-horned goat-like beast, red eyes, matted fur texture via SVG turbulence/noise filter) with separate head layer for lunge; deliberately more realistic than the cast
code_only_remake_requirements.backgrounds: Painted-look village set pieces as layered SVG with noise/grain: grey brick walls, tiled rooftop, iron courtyard gate with bolt, interior bedroom with lattice window, dark brick wall with glowing crack; red door couplets as accent
code_only_remake_requirements.atmosphere: Animated fog layers (blurred noise gradients drifting at 2-3 speeds), vignette, desaturated blue-grey grade with one warm accent per shot, dark shadow sweep across faces
code_only_remake_requirements.camera: Per-shot slow push-in (scale 1.0->1.08), small lateral pans, micro-shake on screams/impacts, diagonal comic split-panel transition, cross-dissolves and fog wipes, fade to black for the 'everything went dark' beat
code_only_remake_requirements.audio_captions: Local TTS (Kokoro) first-person narrator + 2-3 character voices, sped to ~1.35-1.5x (target ~300-350 wpm); word-timed caption chunks of 5-8 words; low drone + stingers on reveals
code_only_remake_requirements.storyboard_density: ~40 shots per 150 s (avg ~3.8 s), expression/pose change every 1-2 s within shots; beat schedule as above with a re-hook every 10-15 s and a hard cut-off cliffhanger
code_only_remake_requirements.series_support: Episode template that starts mid-action and ends mid-line; recurring creature lore bible (name, rules, weakness) to drip across parts
